what: Roper Technologies buys and runs software businesses that lead small, specialised markets: legal case management, construction bidding, freight matching, insurance claims software and laboratory systems. It rarely sells anything it buys.
customers: Law firms, contractors, insurers, freight brokers, hospitals, government agencies and manufacturers, each through a different subsidiary.
money: vertical software for legal, construction, government and healthcare
freight matching, insurance networks and marketplaces
moat: Software that runs a customer's core workflow in a market too small for large vendors to attack, giving very high retention and pricing power.
risks: Growth depends on continuing to find and buy good businesses
Debt of about $10 billion funds that acquisition programme
Return on invested capital of about 6% looks low because goodwill from acquisitions sits in the denominator
Analyst targets imply the shares are already fully valued
opportunities: Revenue grew about 12% last year with a 69% gross margin
Recurring software revenue is the large majority of the total
A long record of raising acquired companies' margins
watch: Organic revenue growth excluding acquisitions, and free cash flow conversion.
